keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «무엇을 해야 하는지 알면 목숨을 구할 수 있다(주제)» 와 «위급한 일이 생기기 전에 대처법을 익히면 나와 다른 사람을 지킬 수 있다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the topic (knowing what to do can save lives) and the conclusion (learning safety steps before an emergency helps you protect yourself and others). The green sentences are the answers.

boxes.a: How knowing safety steps can save lives

boxes.a: The sea pulled back and the water bubbled

boxes.qko: 우리는 무엇을 미리 배워 두어야 하나요?
boxes.qen: What should we learn ahead of time?
boxes.a: Safety steps, before an emergency happens

sumHowto.ko: 먼저 위 세 칸을 보고, 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 고르세요.
sumHowto.en: Look at the three boxes, then choose the right word for each blank.

words: saw something and became aware of it
A huge earthquake under the sea can push up a giant wave
a sudden, strong shaking of the ground
a huge ocean wave caused by an earthquake under the sea
they warned everyone to leave the beach

qs.q: Why were about 100 people from that beach already safe when the tsunami arrived?
qs.qko: 쓰나미가 덮쳤을 때, 그 해변의 약 100명은 왜 이미 안전했나요?
opts: Because Tilly’s parents warned everyone to leave the beach
Because the tourists walked out onto the wet sand
Because the tsunami was too small to reach the shore
evs: Tilly told her parents, and they warned everyone to leave the beach.
Many tourists walked out onto the wet sand to look.
Afterward, use the stairs instead of the elevator, and move to an open space like a park.
Suddenly, she noticed something strange: the sea was pulling back, and the water was bubbling.
why: 틸리가 부모님께 알렸고, 부모님이 모두에게 해변을 떠나라고 경고했어요. 그래서 쓰나미가 덮쳤을 때 사람들은 이미 안전한 곳에 있었어요. 젖은 모래로 걸어 나간 것은 오히려 위험한 행동이었어요.
Tilly told her parents, and they warned everyone to leave the beach, so people were already safe when the wave hit. Walking out onto the wet sand was dangerous.

qs.q: In “the sea was pulling back,” what does “pulling back” mean?
qs.qko: «the sea was pulling back» 에서 «pulling back» 은 무슨 뜻인가요?
evs: Many tourists walked out onto the wet sand to look.
Minutes later, the tsunami crashed onto the shore, but about 100 people from that beach were already safe.
Remember three steps: drop to the floor, cover your head under a strong table, and hold on until the shaking stops.
In December 2004, a ten-year-old British girl named Tilly Smith was on holiday at a beach in Thailand.
why: 바닷물이 빠지자 관광객들이 «젖은 모래» 위로 걸어 나갔어요. 물이 있던 자리가 드러났다는 뜻이니, «pulling back» 은 바닷물이 해변에서 «멀리 물러난다» 는 뜻이에요.
Tourists walked out onto the wet sand, so the water had left that place. «Pulling back» means the sea was moving away from the beach.

qs.q: How did Tilly know that a tsunami might be coming?
qs.qko: 틸리는 쓰나미가 올지도 모른다는 것을 어떻게 알았나요?
opts: She saw the sea pull back and remembered that this often happens before a tsunami
A lifeguard told her parents about a big wave
She saw a giant wave far out at sea
evs: Suddenly, she noticed something strange: the sea was pulling back, and the water was bubbling.
A huge earthquake under the sea can push up a giant wave called a tsunami, and the sea often pulls back just before it arrives.
Many tourists walked out onto the wet sand to look.
Afterward, use the stairs instead of the elevator, and move to an open space like a park.
why: 틸리는 바닷물이 빠져나가는 것을 보았고, 수업에서 «쓰나미가 오기 직전에 바닷물이 빠져나가는 일이 많다» 고 배웠어요. 본 것과 배운 것, 두 문장을 이어야 알 수 있어요.
Tilly saw the sea pulling back, and she had learned that the sea often pulls back just before a tsunami arrives. You need both sentences.

ends: How do countries warn people when a tsunami is coming?
쓰나미가 올 때 나라에서는 사람들에게 어떻게 알릴까?
What should we put in an emergency kit at home?
집에 두는 비상 가방에는 무엇을 넣어야 할까?

write.src: “It is important to <u>learn safety steps</u> because <u>they can save lives in an emergency</u>.”
write.howtoKo: 예문을 틀로 삼아, 빈칸 두 곳을 «중요한 일 + 그 이유» 로 바꿔 영어로 써 보세요.
write.howtoEn: Use the example as a pattern. Write an important action and your reason in English.

write.moreKo: 한 걸음 더: «because» 뒤에 글에서 찾은 사실을 넣어 이유를 분명하게 써 보세요. (예: because the sea pulls back before a tsunami)
write.moreEn: One more step: after «because», use a fact from the text to make your reason clear. (e.g. because the sea pulls back before a tsunami)
